module.title: Unit 2: Environmental Choices: Plastic Pollution & Renewable Habit
module.objective: Mampu mendiskusikan krisis lingkungan dan solusi ramah lingkungan menggunakan passive voice dan cause-effect clauses.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Small Choices, Cleaner Oceans
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Environmental problems, sustainable choices, and renewable energy

content.summary: Read about a student group that investigates plastic pollution and tries simple ways to protect the environment. You will practise finding the main idea and important details, and notice how passive voice and cause-and-effect phrases explain environmental problems and solutions.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use the passive voice to focus on what happens to something: Plastic bottles are collected. Use because with a subject and verb to give a reason, and because of with a noun phrase. Use as a result, therefore, and so to connect a cause with its effect.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn words for plastic waste, ecosystems, renewable energy, biodegradable materials, carbon footprints, and sustainable choices.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the title and first sentences to understand the main idea. Then scan the text for names, actions, reasons, and results. Look for passive verb forms and cause-and-effect connectors.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a B1 text about plastic pollution and practical environmental choices.
Locate details about the causes of pollution and the actions taken by a student group.
Recognize passive voice forms used to describe environmental problems and solutions.
Identify cause-and-effect relationships signalled by because, because of, as a result, and therefore.

contextWarmup.prompt: Which choice can help reduce the number of plastic bags people use?
options: Carry a reusable shopping bag
Ask for two plastic bags for every item
Leave used bags on the beach
contextWarmup.explanation: A reusable bag can be used many times, so people do not need a new plastic bag for each shopping trip.

rules: Use be plus a past participle to form the passive voice: Plastic waste is collected. The focus is on the waste, not on the person collecting it.

Use because or since before a clause with a subject and verb: The river is polluted because factories release waste. Use because of before a noun phrase: The river is polluted because of factory waste.
Use as a result, therefore, consequently, or so to show an effect: The town uses solar power; as a result, it burns less fuel.

commonTrap.explanation: Do not use because of before a complete clause. Because of needs a noun or noun phrase, while because is followed by a subject and verb.
commonTrap.wrong: The beach is dirty because of people leave plastic there.
commonTrap.correct: The beach is dirty because people leave plastic there. / The beach is dirty because of plastic waste.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Passive Voice and Cause and Effect
grammarFormulas.description: Use these sentence blocks to practise describing environmental actions, reasons, and results:

complements.text: as a result, less waste reaches the sea

items.exampleSentence: Plastic pollution can harm animals in the sea.
The school gets some of its power from renewable energy.
Cycling to school can lower your carbon footprint.
Plastic waste can damage a coastal ecosystem.
The students are looking for sustainable ways to travel.
She takes a reusable bottle to school.
The group sorted the waste into different bins.
A solar panel on the roof provides power on sunny days.

paragraphs: At Brookside School, a group called the Green Team meets every Friday. Last month, its members studied plastic pollution in their local river. They learned that bags and bottles are carried from streets into the water when it rains. Small pieces of plastic can then be eaten by fish and birds. The team wanted to find out how students could help.

First, the students counted the rubbish near the river. They found many takeaway cups and food wrappers, so they spoke to nearby cafés. Two cafés now give discounts to customers who bring reusable cups. The school canteen has also stopped giving out plastic straws. These changes were made because the team shared its findings with local people.

The group has started a bottle collection, too. Clean bottles are sorted and sent to a recycling centre. Some families have replaced plastic bags with biodegradable ones, although reusable bags are still a better choice because they can be used many times. As a result of these small actions, less rubbish is left around the school and river.

The Green Team also asked the school to install solar panels. The project has not started yet, but the head teacher is checking the cost. Solar panels can provide renewable energy, so the school may use less electricity from fuels that release carbon dioxide. The students know that one project will not solve every problem. However, they believe that sustainable habits can make a difference when many people take part.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe how a school group takes action on local environmental problems
To explain how to open a café near a river
To compare different types of fish
questions.answer: To describe how a school group takes action on local environmental problems
questions.explanation: The passage follows the Green Team as it studies plastic pollution and suggests local changes.

questions.question: How can bags and bottles reach the river?
options: They are carried from streets into the water when it rains
They are brought there by the school canteen
They fall from solar panels
questions.answer: They are carried from streets into the water when it rains
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says rain carries bags and bottles from the streets into the water.

questions.question: What can happen to small pieces of plastic in the river?
options: Fish and birds can eat them
They turn into solar panels
They clean the water
questions.answer: Fish and birds can eat them
questions.explanation: The passage says that small pieces of plastic can be eaten by fish and birds.

questions.question: Why did the Green Team speak to nearby cafés?
options: It found many takeaway cups and food wrappers near the river
The cafés asked the students to install solar panels
The students wanted to sell reusable bags
questions.answer: It found many takeaway cups and food wrappers near the river
questions.explanation: The students counted rubbish and found many cups and wrappers before speaking to the cafés.

questions.question: What do two cafés offer customers who bring reusable cups?
options: Discounts
Free solar panels
Biodegradable bottles
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says that two cafés give discounts to customers with reusable cups.

questions.question: What happens to the clean bottles collected by the group?
options: They are sorted and sent to a recycling centre
They are left beside the river
They are used as plastic straws
questions.answer: They are sorted and sent to a recycling centre
questions.explanation: The passage states that clean bottles are sorted and sent to a recycling centre.

questions.question: Why are reusable bags described as a better choice than biodegradable bags?
options: They can be used many times
They are made by the cafés
They can produce renewable energy
questions.answer: They can be used many times
questions.explanation: The passage explains that reusable bags are a better choice because they can be used many times.

questions.question: Has the school started installing solar panels?
options: No, the head teacher is still checking the cost
Yes, the panels are already working
No, because the students do not want renewable energy
questions.answer: No, the head teacher is still checking the cost
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says the project has not started yet and the head teacher is checking the cost.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Clean bottles are sorted and sent to a recycling centre', what does the passive voice focus on?
options: The bottles and what happens to them
The name of the person who sorts them
The cost of the recycling centre
questions.answer: The bottles and what happens to them
questions.explanation: The passive form 'are sorted and sent' focuses on the bottles. The people doing the actions are not named.

questions.question: What does 'As a result' introduce in the third paragraph?
options: The effect of the group's small actions
A new cause of plastic pollution
A question about the cafés
questions.answer: The effect of the group's small actions
questions.explanation: The phrase introduces the result: less rubbish is left around the school and river.

content.summary: Learn how to listen for passive structures and cause-effect links when people discuss environmental topics. In casual university discussions, speakers frequently link final consonants to following vowels and soften passive auxiliary verbs like 'are' and 'been'.
learningObjectives: Catch the main points of a conversation about plastic pollution and green habits.
Recognize passive verb forms used to report environmental facts.
Identify consonant-to-vowel linking in fast conversational English.

keyPhrases.note: Commonly used in passive sentences to describe waste disposal.
Present continuous passive showing ongoing environmental destruction.
Refers to power from natural resources like wind and sun.
An idiomatic phrase used to express having a significant effect.

connectedSpeech.note: The final /t/ sound connects smoothly to the following short /ɪ/ vowel.
The stop consonant /t/ links directly into the vowel /e/ of every.
The final /t/ in 'that' carries over to the vowel in 'on'.
The final /d/ sound is elided before the bilabial consonant /b/.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Cleaner Choices, Healthier Oceans

content.summary: Use passive voice to focus on what happens to the environment. Use cause-and-effect clauses to explain why a problem happens and what happens next. Build a clear paragraph by stating a problem, giving its cause, and describing a practical solution.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Focus on the Effect with Passive Voice
blueprintItems.formula: Subject receiving the action + be (am/is/are/was/were) + past participle (+ by agent)
blueprintItems.example: Millions of plastic bottles are thrown away each year.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Explain a Cause
blueprintItems.formula: Because / Since / As + subject + verb, + result; Because of + noun phrase, + result
blueprintItems.example: Because people use too many plastic bags, more rubbish ends up in rivers.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Connect an Effect to a Result
blueprintItems.formula: Cause or effect; as a result / therefore / consequently / so + related result
blueprintItems.example: Sea water is becoming warmer; as a result, some coral reefs are being damaged.

mechanicsRules.rule: In the passive voice, use the correct form of be before the past participle.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Plastic bottles are throw into the sea.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Plastic bottles are thrown into the sea.
mechanicsRules.why: The passive form needs a form of be and a past participle. The past participle of throw is thrown.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use because before a full clause, and use because of before a noun or noun phrase.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Because of people leave rubbish on the beach, birds may eat it.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Because people leave rubbish on the beach, birds may eat it.
mechanicsRules.why: People leave rubbish is a full clause, so because is the correct choice.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma after a cause clause at the beginning of a sentence. Start a new sentence with a capital letter and finish it with suitable punctuation.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Because forests are cut down many animals lose their homes
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Because forests are cut down, many animals lose their homes.
mechanicsRules.why: The comma separates the opening cause clause from the result, and the full sentence needs a capital letter and a full stop.

sampleSentences.en: Old fishing nets are sometimes left in the sea.
sampleSentences.id: Jaring ikan lama terkadang ditinggalkan di laut.

sampleSentences.en: Because some towns do not recycle plastic, more rubbish is sent to landfill.
sampleSentences.id: Karena beberapa kota tidak mendaur ulang plastik, lebih banyak sampah dikirim ke tempat pembuangan akhir.

sampleSentences.en: Because of pollution from cars, the air in busy city centres can become unhealthy.
sampleSentences.id: Karena polusi dari mobil, udara di pusat kota yang ramai dapat menjadi tidak sehat.
sampleSentences.focus: Because of followed by a noun phrase

sampleSentences.en: Our school uses solar panels; as a result, it needs less electricity from the grid.
sampleSentences.id: Sekolah kami menggunakan panel surya; akibatnya, sekolah membutuhkan lebih sedikit listrik dari jaringan listrik.

mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Plastic bags are used in many shops because shoppers forget to bring their own bags.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Kantong plastik digunakan di banyak toko karena pembeli lupa membawa tas sendiri.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Begin with a capital letter, use be plus a past participle for the passive voice, and end with a full stop.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: because of plastic waste is left on beaches turtles can be harmed
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Because plastic waste is left on beaches, turtles can be harmed.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Karena sampah plastik ditinggalkan di pantai, penyu dapat terluka.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use because before a full clause, add a comma after an opening cause clause, and use a capital letter and full stop.

mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Wind turbines produce clean energy; as a result, less coal is burned.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Turbin angin menghasilkan energi bersih; akibatnya, lebih sedikit batu bara dibakar.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use a capital letter, separate two complete ideas with a semicolon, and place a comma after as a result.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Explain a Plastic Pollution Problem
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write four to five sentences about plastic pollution. Describe one problem with passive voice, explain a cause with because or because of, and give one result.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Plastic bags are often left on beaches. Because some people do not use rubbish bins, the bags can reach the sea. As a result, sea animals may eat them. People can help by carrying reusable bags.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Write your sentences about plastic pollution here...

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Recommend a Renewable Energy Choice
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write four to five sentences about a renewable energy choice for a home, school, or town. Include one passive sentence, explain a cause, and connect it to a result.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Solar panels are installed on our school roof. Because the school receives plenty of sunlight, the panels can make useful energy. As a result, less electricity is needed from coal. The school could also save money over time.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Write your sentences about renewable energy here...

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the active sentence in the passive voice. Keep the present simple tense.
practicumQuestions.promptText: People throw away millions of plastic bottles every year.
practicumQuestions.hint: Make millions of plastic bottles the subject. Use are and the past participle of throw.
targetAnswers: Millions of plastic bottles are thrown away every year.
Millions of plastic bottles are thrown away every year by people.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use the object of the active sentence as the new subject. The present simple passive uses are plus the past participle thrown.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the ideas using because.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Plastic waste enters the sea. People leave rubbish on the beach.
practicumQuestions.hint: Put the cause after because and the result in the other clause.
targetAnswers: Because people leave rubbish on the beach, plastic waste enters the sea.
Plastic waste enters the sea because people leave rubbish on the beach.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because introduces a cause clause. When that clause comes first, put a comma before the result clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Join the ideas using because of.
practicumQuestions.promptText: The river is polluted. Plastic rubbish is in the water.
practicumQuestions.hint: After because of, use a noun phrase, not a full subject and verb clause.
targetAnswers: The river is polluted because of the plastic rubbish in the water.
Because of the plastic rubbish in the water, the river is polluted.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because of is followed by a noun phrase. The plastic rubbish in the water is a noun phrase.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: because or because of.
practicumQuestions.promptText: _____ many homes use solar panels, less electricity is needed from the grid.
practicumQuestions.hint: The words after the gap have a subject and a verb.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use because before a full clause. Many homes use solar panels has a subject and a verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with because of.
practicumQuestions.promptText: _____ rising sea temperatures, some coral reefs are being damaged.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the linker that must be followed by a noun phrase.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Rising sea temperatures is a noun phrase, so because of is the correct linker.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the result sentence with as a result.
practicumQuestions.promptText: More homes are using solar energy; _____, less coal is burned.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the three-word linker and place a comma after it.
practicumQuestions.explanation: As a result introduces the consequence of the first idea. Put a comma after the linker.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the capital letters, passive form, and punctuation.
practicumQuestions.promptText: old fishing nets are leave in the sea and turtles are trap
practicumQuestions.hint: Use are plus the past participles left and trapped.
targetAnswers: Old fishing nets are left in the sea, and turtles are trapped.
Old fishing nets are left in the sea and turtles are trapped.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Start the sentence with a capital letter, use the past participles left and trapped after are, and finish with a full stop.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the linker and punctuation in the sentence.
practicumQuestions.promptText: because of factories release waste many rivers are polluted
practicumQuestions.hint: Factories release waste is a full clause, so use because.
targetAnswers: Because factories release waste, many rivers are polluted.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use because before a full clause. Add a comma after the opening cause clause, capitalize the first word, and finish with a full stop.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write one sentence using the passive voice to describe plastic pollution.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Explain what can happen to plastic waste in the ocean.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use a form of be and a past participle, for example, carried or eaten.
targetAnswers: Plastic waste is carried into the ocean by rivers.
Plastic rubbish is eaten by some sea animals.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A correct answer uses a form of be followed by a past participle and gives a clear fact about plastic pollution. Other correct sentences are possible.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write two connected sentences about a renewable energy choice. Use because in one sentence and therefore or as a result in the other.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Suggest a renewable energy choice and explain one effect.
practicumQuestions.hint: Give a cause with because, then use the second sentence to show a result.
targetAnswers: Because our school gets plenty of sunlight, solar panels can make electricity. As a result, less energy is needed from coal.
Wind turbines are used because our area is often windy. Therefore, less fossil fuel is burned.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A good response names a renewable energy choice, gives a clear cause with because, and connects it to a result with therefore or as a result. Other correct answers are possible.

content.summary: Practise discussing plastic pollution and practical environmental choices. Use the passive voice to describe problems and changes, and use cause-and-effect clauses to explain why actions matter.
content.audioGuidance: Speak at a steady pace and finish each thought clearly. Stress the key words in a sentence. Let your voice fall at the end of statements. Use a rising tone for yes-or-no questions, and a falling tone for information questions.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Say the vowel in words such as plastic and energy clearly. Keep long vowels in words such as clean and green steady, rather than cutting them short.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.explanation: Listen for the strong syllable in longer words, such as re-NEW-a-ble and sus-TAIN-a-ble. Make that syllable clearer and slightly stronger.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.explanation: Give more stress to the main idea words, such as plastic, oceans, energy, and reduce. Say small grammar words more lightly.

pillars.name: Clear Explanations
pillars.explanation: Use because to give a reason and so to show a result. Pause briefly between the problem, the cause, and the solution.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The main stress is on the first syllable in pollution and the second syllable in ecosystem.
Both words have four syllables. Stress NEW in renewable and TAIN in sustainable.
Stress the first syllable of biodegradable. In carbon footprint, stress the first syllable of each word.
The main stress is on the second syllable in both alternative and environment.

drills.targetText: Plastic pollution is harming ocean ecosystems.
drills.focus: Word stress in plastic pollution and ecosystem
drills.hint: Keep the sentence steady and make the main words clear.

drills.targetText: Solar energy is used because it is renewable.
drills.phonetic: /ˈsəʊlə ˈenədʒi ɪz juːzd bɪˈkɒz ɪt ɪz rɪˈnjuːəbl/
drills.focus: Passive voice and the cause clause with because
drills.hint: Link is used smoothly, then pause briefly before because.

drills.targetText: Biodegradable bags can reduce plastic waste.
drills.focus: Long word stress and clear consonants
drills.hint: Say biodegradable in parts, then join the parts smoothly.

drills.targetText: We take the bus, so our carbon footprint is smaller.
drills.phonetic: /wiː teɪk ðə bʌs səʊ aʊə ˈkɑːbən ˈfʊtprɪnt ɪz ˈsmɔːlə/
drills.hint: Give a short pause before so, then stress carbon footprint and smaller.

roleplay.context: You are discussing plastic waste and cleaner energy at a school environment club meeting.

turns.speaker: Club Leader
turns.text: Plastic waste is often found near the river. What could our school do about it?
turns.translation: Sampah plastik sering ditemukan di dekat sungai. Apa yang bisa dilakukan sekolah kita untuk mengatasinya?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: We could provide more recycling bins because bottles are often thrown away with general waste.
turns.translation: Kita bisa menyediakan lebih banyak tempat sampah daur ulang karena botol sering dibuang bersama sampah umum.

turns.speaker: Club Leader
turns.text: Good idea. Could we also use renewable energy at school?
turns.translation: Ide bagus. Bisakah kita juga menggunakan energi terbarukan di sekolah?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: Yes, solar panels could be installed on the roof, so less electricity would come from fossil fuels.
turns.translation: Ya, panel surya bisa dipasang di atap, sehingga lebih sedikit listrik berasal dari bahan bakar fosil.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about a time you noticed plastic pollution and what happened next.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell a short story about plastic pollution in a place you know.
storyPoints: Where you saw plastic waste and what it looked like
How the waste affected people, animals, or the ecosystem
What action was taken or could be taken to improve the situation
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Plastic waste was left near the river, so our class collected it and put it in recycling bins.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈplæstɪk weɪst wəz left nɪə ðə ˈrɪvə/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Tell the events in order. Use the passive voice to describe what was done and so or because to explain a result.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about an environmental habit you have tried or would like to try.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a sustainable habit and explain why it could help.
storyPoints: Name a habit, such as using a reusable bottle or taking public transport
Explain how it can reduce waste or your carbon footprint
Say what might make the habit easy or difficult for you
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I take public transport because it can reduce my carbon footprint and save fuel.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ teɪk ˈpʌblɪk ˈtrænspɔːt bɪˈkɒz ɪt kən rɪˈdjuːs maɪ ˈkɑːbən ˈfʊtprɪnt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give a clear example and explain its effect using a cause-and-effect clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Answer the club leader and suggest one practical way to reduce plastic waste at school.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The club leader asks what the school should do about single-use plastic.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are speaking with a school environment club leader who wants to reduce single-use plastic.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student who can suggest a realistic change and explain why it would help.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Reusable bottles could be encouraged because fewer plastic bottles would be thrown away.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /riːˈjuːzəbl ˈbɒtlz kʊd bi ɪnˈkʌrɪdʒd bɪˈkɒz fjuːə ˈplæstɪk ˈbɒtlz wʊd bi ˈθrəʊn əˈweɪ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Make a suggestion and use the passive voice to explain what would happen.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Explain the problem and suggest a suitable replacement for plastic bags.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A shop owner asks whether biodegradable bags are a good choice.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are speaking with a local shop owner who is choosing bags for customers.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a customer who supports biodegradable alternatives and can explain their benefit.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Biodegradable bags may be a better choice because they can break down naturally.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˌbaɪəʊdɪˈɡreɪdəbl bæɡz meɪ bi ə ˈbetə tʃɔɪs bɪˈkɒz ðeɪ kən breɪk daʊn ˈnætʃərəli/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give your opinion and use because to explain your reason.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Respond to a neighbour who is asking about solar panels.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your neighbour asks how renewable energy could help the community.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You and a neighbour are discussing whether solar panels could be used in your community.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a resident who can explain one benefit of renewable energy in simple terms.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Solar panels could be installed on more homes, so less energy would need to come from fossil fuels.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈsəʊlə ˈpænəlz kʊd bi ɪnˈstɔːld ɒn mɔː həʊmz səʊ les ˈenədʒi wʊd niːd tə kʌm frəm ˈfɒsəl fjʊəlz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describe a possible change using the passive voice, then explain its result with so.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a live roleplay call. Discuss a local environmental problem and agree on one action.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A community volunteer asks how residents can protect a local ecosystem.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are talking with a community volunteer about pollution near a local park or river.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a resident who wants to protect the local ecosystem and can suggest a shared action.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The river should be cleaned regularly because plastic can harm animals and plants.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈrɪvə ʃʊd bi kliːnd ˈreɡjələli bɪˈkɒz ˈplæstɪk kən hɑːm ˈænɪməlz ən plɑːnts/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Suggest an action and connect it to a clear reason.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say a complete sentence using the words renewable energy and carbon footprint.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Explain one way renewable energy can help reduce a carbon footprint.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Renewable energy can reduce a community's carbon footprint because it produces fewer emissions.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈenədʒi kən rɪˈdjuːs ə kəˈmjuːnɪtiz ˈkɑːbən ˈfʊtprɪnt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use both key terms in a sentence and explain their connection.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Describe a change using the passive voice, then add a result with so or a reason with because.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Explain what could be done with plastic bottles and why it would help.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Plastic bottles should be recycled because this reduces waste.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈplæstɪk ˈbɒtlz ʃʊd bi ˌriːˈsaɪkəld bɪˈkɒz ðɪs rɪˈdjuːsɪz weɪst/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use a passive form such as should be recycled and give a clear reason or result.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say sustainable, biodegradable, and renewable energy. Make the stressed syllables clear.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Repeat the environmental words with natural syllable stress.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Sustainable choices include biodegradable products and renewable energy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Stress TAIN in sustainable, GRAD in biodegradable, and NEW in renewable.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say one yes-or-no question with rising intonation, then say one information question with falling intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ask a question about recycling and a question about the cause of plastic pollution.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Can plastic bottles be recycled? Why is plastic pollution harmful?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /kən ˈplæstɪk ˈbɒtlz bi ˌriːˈsaɪkəld? waɪ ɪz ˈplæstɪk pəˈluːʃən ˈhɑːmfəl/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice rise at the end of the yes-or-no question. Let it fall at the end of the question beginning with why.
